failure_summary.description: The answer repeated or extended a word from the clue instead of giving the referent: 'Treaty of Paris (1815)' for 'his final defeat' (Napoleon), 'University of Wisconsin-Superior' when the clue already says 'at Superior', and 'Sultan of Brunei' with the title attached.

There is no guidance for clues that are a bare name or title (answer the country or realm), or that carry a parenthetical identifier such as '(U.S. president, '81-'89)'. The agent took 'Starr' from the neighbouring archive clue instead of Reagan.

'The second S in LSUS' asks what an abbreviation letter stands for. The agent answered the city tied to LSU (Baton Rouge) instead of expanding the abbreviation to 'LSU Shreveport' as the passages show.

'This current king of Jordan' was resolved to the present holder (Abdullah II). The clue's concrete facts (Harrow and Sandhurst) match King Hussein, and the word 'current' reflects when the clue was written.
A qualifier was added to the base name: 'sea lamprey' where 'lamprey' was wanted.

patch.reasoning: Several failures come from the answer tracking clue wording or a salient context entity instead of the referent. I add four short, targeted rules and avoid the large bundles that were rejected earlier. (1) Pronouns and clue-contained name parts: the answer is the person or parent entity, never the named event, nor a name that repeats the clue's words. (2) Bare name or title clues, and parenthetical identifiers. (3) Abbreviation-letter clues. (4) Outdated time words in the clue, and base names without extra qualifiers.

edits.target: Other named entities in the clue are anchors, never the answer.
edits.content:
- A possessive pronoun ('his', 'her', 'their') or 'this man/woman' next to a named event, treaty, battle, book or work means the answer is the PERSON behind it, never the thing named in the clue: 'The 1815 Treaty of Paris was signed after his final defeat at Waterloo' -> 'Napoleon', not 'Treaty of Paris'. Sanity check: if your answer repeats the clue's own distinctive words, it is probably wrong.
- If the clue already supplies a branch, campus, city or qualifier ('this state university at Superior, not Madison'), the answer is the base/parent name without it ('University of Wisconsin', not 'University of Wisconsin-Superior').

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content:
- A clue that is only a person's name and title ('Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah') is a category-style clue. Answer with the country, realm or organization the passages tie him to, in bare form ('Brunei', not 'Sultan of Brunei').
- A parenthetical identifier in the clue ('seen here: (U.S. president, '81-'89)') describes the answer, which here is the person who fits it ('Ronald Reagan'). When the clue refers to an unseen picture, ignore that part and answer from the description. Archive pages list many clues one after another, so never take the answer from a neighbouring clue ('Starr' came from the preceding clue).

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content:
- Abbreviation-letter clues ('The second "S" in LSUS stands for this city'): find the full expanded name in the passages ('LSU Shreveport') and answer the word that letter stands for ('Shreveport'). Do not answer with the place most associated with the main part of the abbreviation (Baton Rouge for LSU).
- Time words in a clue ('current', 'present', 'new', 'latest') reflect when the clue was written, often decades ago. Pick the entity whose concrete facts (schooling, deeds, dates) match the clue, even if a later holder of the title exists: 'This current king of Jordan ... Harrow & Sandhurst' -> 'King Hussein' (the passages' form), not Abdullah II.
- Answer with the base common name, without added qualifiers such as 'sea', 'common' or 'American', unless the clue itself includes them: 'lamprey', not 'sea lamprey'.
